Become your best
Welcome to Claremont School in East Sussex, UK
Supporting lifelong learning
Every child is seen, valued, and supported to achieve their potential — we embrace differences as strengths, with close personal support from experienced tutors and support staff.
Academic achievement
Claremont outperforms other independent schools locally. Students achieve outstanding results in their GCSEs, A Levels and BTECs, accessing the world's leading universities and their chosen careers.
Home-from-home boarding experience

International Football Academy

Award-winning performing arts programme
Students develop their skills through a double national award-winning programme with specialised training in music, dance and drama, leading to either an A Level, BTEC, LAMDA or ABRSM qualification.
Multilingual learning
Students learn major global languages including French, Spanish, Mandarin and German. International students benefit from our accredited and highly successful EAL programme.
Students build their communication skills, digital-fluency and self-leadership through our Skills Passport and a Life Skills framework backed by Camtree and Hughes Hall, University of Cambridge.
English language programmes
From two-week immersion courses to a specialist one-year GCSE course, we specialise in providing an English language option for all levels of learning.
Where confidence grows
At our independent school in East Sussex, students connect with peers around the world through global skill-building programmes and learning opportunities as part of the International Schools Partnership network.
Technology enhanced learning
Prepare to succeed in a tech-driven world using the latest tools and software which enable students to learn, experiment and grow.

Strong academic results begin with students who feel challenged, supported and engaged in learning. Students across ISP schools consistently achieve results above local and international benchmarks through learning experiences that challenge thinking, deepen understanding and help every learner keep getting better.
Students are growing up in a world shaped by rapid technological change, uncertainty and challenges we cannot yet predict. To thrive, they need the curiosity to question, the confidence to adapt, the ability to collaborate and the resilience to keep learning throughout life. International Schools Partnership – ISP has partnered with Hughes Hall, University of Cambridge through Camtree and DEFI to embed life competencies into everyday learning experiences across ISP schools worldwide.
Language opens doors to new cultures, perspectives and opportunities. Students across ISP schools develop proficiency in multiple world languages while continuing to strengthen their home or first language. Through meaningful learning experiences and international collaboration, students build the confidence to communicate across cultures and thrive in global environments.
International learning experiences help students see beyond their own environment and understand the world from different perspectives. Students across ISP schools take part in unique collaborations, exchanges, competitions and global experiences that encourage curiosity, teamwork and independent thinking. Working with global partners, these life-changing opportunities help students build confidence, strengthen relationships and adapt to new experiences across cultures and countries.
Every student’s future pathway is different and through our Future Pathways programme, families are supported by specialist counsellors and advisors who guide subject choices, university applications and career decisions with personalised support throughout the learning journey. University fairs, global experts and our A–Z Speaker Series help students explore emerging careers and future industries with confidence. Students benefit from exclusive ISP scholarships and opportunities with some of the world’s most recognised institutions.
Admissions journey - UK students
Ask the most important questions for your family about our curriculum, fees and scholarships.
Tour our school in person and see learning in action. Meet the senior leadership team during an Open Day or schedule a private appointment with our admissions team.
Apply for a day or boarding place at Claremont. This involves completing our application form, the submission of recent school reports and payment of a registration fee.
Your child will meet fellow classmates, immerse in creative, sporting and academic activities and take an assessment in non-exam conditions.
Receive a conditional offer
We'll send a conditional offer letter after all application requirements have been met.
Secure your child's place
Complete the necessary forms and make a deposit. Once we receive your acceptance form, we'll contact your current school (if independent) for a reference.
Welcome to Claremont!
We'll send you a welcome pack with all the information you will need for your child to begin their learning journey at Claremont.
Admissions journey - international students
Speak with our Admissions team who will share tailored guidance about the school, boarding and UK entry requirements. We'll arrange a virtual meeting with a Senior Leader.
If possible, we welcome you to tour the school in person, or schedule a private appointment with our admissions team.
Apply for a boarding place
Complete a Boarding Application Form and provide copies of child and parents' passports and student's birth certificate and school reports for the past two years
Complete assessments
Your child will take an online English language test. If applicable, we'll arrange a virtual meeting with our special educational needs team or the Football Academy Director.
Receive a conditional offer
Once all of the above is completed satisfactorily, we'll issue an offer letter, outlining any conditions for entry and any potential scholarship award.
Return the required forms and payment to secure your child's place. If you require a visa to study in the UK, we'll help you obtain the required document (CAS) with the assistance of our specialist consultants.

Drama Teacher & LAMDA Specialist
Sarah encourages her students to create opportunities for themselves to do what they love and not to wait for others to make it happen, with empowerment on and off stage at the heart of what she does. Under her leadership, Claremont’s Performing Arts department has thrived, fostering creativity and student leadership in a vibrant and award winning Performing Arts programme.
Sarah trained as an actor at the Royal Welsh College of Music and Drama (Theatre Studies – Acting BA Hons) and Manchester Metropolitan University (PGCE). After leaving Drama school Sarah was part of a Theatre company called Hot Wax, taking comedy sketch shows to Fringe Festivals throughout the UK. Sarah has worked for the National Theatre Education Department, Half Moon Young People’s Theatre and has appeared in new work for the Royal Court. Sarah believes in the power of taking risks, often saying to her students, “Just have a go…who knows what might happen!”.
Beth has been dancing since she was three years old and hasn’t stopped! First training with Redhurst School of Dance, Sussex, Beth pursued a BA Hons Dance degree at Liverpool John Moores and Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts for Dance Technique in Contemporary, Ballet and Jazz. She holds Masters credits specialising in Dance in Education from the University of Bedfordshire. Following this, she worked as a professional dancer in London working on projects involving a variety of dance styles for events including promotional work for the CCPR (representing Dance affiliations) and teaching baby ballet at the weekend. This followed her path to obtain a PGCE from Brighton University.
Beth holds a Diploma In Dance Education with the Imperial Society of Teacher of Dance in the Classical Ballet genre. She has been examining for the AQA exam board for the last 12 years for GCSE Dance. Beth has a dog called Murphy and enjoys all things creative!
Rebecca has played French horn and piano from a young age, and ultimately went on to study Music at the University of Manchester. Rebecca was Head of Music at Mascalls school for eight years before taking a career break after having two children and acquiring a dog, Wilson.
Rebecca is passionate about ensemble playing and is Chairperson of Penshurst Choral Society, principal horn of Bacchus Wind Orchestra, plays regularly with Penshurst Brass Quintet and sings with The 1839 Consort.
Lucy trained at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art and earned a BA in English from the University of Sussex, specialising in Global Cinema and Staging the Renaissance. She is also a National Youth Theatre alumni. Her performance career includes Jeff Wayne’s The War of the Worlds (London) as well as other performances in the UK and USA. Previously, Lucy won the one-minute round at MonologueSlam and co-created Proving It, a two-woman show at Theatre By The Lake. Her theatre company, Big Blanket Productions, has received multiple nominations at the Manchester Fringe Awards, including Best Play, Best Director and Best Actor for This Wide Night.
Lucy works as a voice actor and is best known for her role as Rhaya in the award-winning sci-fi audiobook The Dex Legacy. Her industry experience includes behind-the-scenes roles, such as script reader for Sky Arts and operational and backstage work for the BBC, ITV and The Royal Albert Hall.
Natasha studied Creative Music Production (BMus) at the University of Huddersfield, specialising in classical performance and sound design for film. Following this, she completed a Masters in Music (Composition) at the University of Nottingham. Natasha has taught Music and Music Technology for over ten years, and also has experience as a freelance record producer. A classically-trained violinist, Natasha performs regularly with the Sussex Concert Orchestra and Eastbourne Symphony Orchestra.
Aside from music, Natasha enjoys countryside walks with her family and two German Shepherds, as well as baking, archery and netball.
Claire trained as an actor at Mountview Theatre School before specialising at the Desmond Jones School of Mime and Physical Theatre. She worked professionally for the English Shakespeare Company, Oxfordshire Touring Theatre and Young Shakespeare. Claire travelled all over the world, often being cast as energetic young boys, sprites and an array of small furry animals.
Claire used her skills in the corporate world as a facilitator and workshop leader freelancing for a variety of creative agencies including So Just Add Water, Purple Monster and Identity. Through her love of Shakespeare Claire began to work in schools running Shakespeare workshops.
Claire is a LAMDA specialist and has been teaching the syllabus for over 20 years with students from all over the world. When Claire is not at work, she can often be found at The Globe (one of her favourite places), walking her Scottie along the seafront or watching her son’s band!
Future-proofing young professionals
Performing Arts is like no other area of their student life - it is a doorway to the fullest expression of themselves - something of profound value to our students.
We focus on the whole person in the Performing Arts, everything that a student is, everything they stand for and against, their interests, their cultures and experiences all feed into the work that they produce and how they reflect upon the work we create.
The skills needed and developed in the creative processes alter each and every young person - they find both camaraderie and self reliance, leaving them feeling gently held and fully empowered. We treat our young performers as professionals and professionals is what they become.

What is SEND?
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) cover a range of learning challenges, including:
Communication & Interaction
Cognition & Learning
Social, Emotional & Mental Health
Sensory & Physical Difficulties
Our Approach
Early identification of additional needs.
Quality First Teaching in every classroom – lessons are adapted to meet different needs, with high expectations for all pupils.
Personalised programmes of support that may include small group or 1:1 interventions, therapies, nurture groups, and specialist resources.
Pupil Profiles created in partnership with parents, pupils, and staff, reviewed at least three times a year.
Collaboration with parents, carers, and external professionals, including Educational Psychologists, Speech & Language Therapists, and other specialists.
Alignment with the SEND Code of Practice (2015) and ISI inspection standards.
Learning Support Provision
Our dedicated Learning Support team has a wide range of SEND specialisms and qualifications. Together with teaching staff, they provide:
Multi-sensory learning strategies to build independence.
Individual Support Plans with clear targets, regularly reviewed
Targeted interventions in literacy, numeracy, and social-emotional skills.
Monitoring of progress, with assessments and referrals if further support is required.
Specialist Input from Educational Psychologists, Speech & Language Therapists, and other professionals.

Where Talent Meets Opportunity: Claremont's Award-Winning Performing Arts Programme
Parents know that choosing the right school for a child who loves performing arts is never simple
You want a place where your child can grow with confidence, but you also need reassurance that their education will be academically strong, broad, and future-focused.
Claremont offers that balance: specialist creative training within a full independent school, so your child does not have to choose between excellence in the classroom and excellence on stage.
More Than a School Play: What Makes a Specialist Performing Arts Programme Different
What separates a genuine specialist performing arts education from standard drama or music lessons is depth, expertise, and purpose. At Claremont, students learn from professional practitioners with real-world experience, work towards formal qualifications at every level, and train in purpose-built facilities designed to support serious development. Just as importantly, they are treated as emerging professionals, with high expectations, real responsibility, and a culture where performing arts is integrated into school life rather than added on as an extra.
Three Disciplines, One Exceptional Programme
Claremont’s programme brings together drama, dance, and music in one cohesive offer, available both as formal academic subjects and as enrichment opportunities that help every student grow. From Prep through Sixth Form, the programme is led by industry practitioners who understand how to nurture technique, confidence, and creativity at every stage. That commitment has earned Claremont national recognition, including double Independent School Association Award wins for Performing Arts. You do not need to arrive at a specialist level to benefit; this is a programme that develops young people from any starting point, helping each child discover what they can achieve.
Professional-Standard Facilities That Inspire Excellence
Claremont’s performing arts spaces are designed to do more than support lessons. They help students think and work like emerging artists. The 220-seat theatre gives young performers the chance to experience lighting, sound, audience response, and stagecraft in a setting that feels authentic, while the purpose-built dance studio and dedicated music suite create the kind of focused environment where technique can truly develop. Students rehearse, record, perform, and are assessed in professional settings, not repurposed halls, which makes a real difference to confidence and standards. They also benefit from workshops led by industry professionals and visits to external venues, including Pineapple Studios, broadening their understanding of what excellent performance training looks like beyond school.
Real Qualifications, Real Destinations
For parents, outcomes matter and Claremont’s programme is built with that in mind. Students work towards recognised qualifications through LAMDA as well as formal academic pathways, so their progress is measured and meaningful at every stage. That combination of training and achievement helps open doors, with Claremont students regularly gaining entry to specialist schools and colleges including Mountview, RADA, Performers and Bird. It is serious preparation for the next step, not just hobby-level enrichment.
Boarding Options for Dedicated Young Performers
Claremont also offers full and weekly boarding from age 10, giving dedicated young performers the stability and structure they need to thrive. For families balancing busy schedules or travelling commitments, this creates a practical way for students to combine specialist training with boarding life in a supportive environment. The daily routine is carefully organised to support both academic progress and creative development, helping students stay focused, build independence, and make the most of every opportunity.
Developing the Whole Person, Not Just the Performer
At Claremont, performing arts is about shaping the whole person, not only polishing a set of stage skills. Students bring their interests, cultures, experiences, and values into the room, and those influences become part of their creative work. They are encouraged to develop as artists with perspective, not just as performers who follow instruction. Alongside technical growth, they build camaraderie and self-reliance, learning how to collaborate with others while also trusting their own voice. They are treated as professionals, and over time, they grow into professionals. This balance of care, challenge, and expectation leaves students feeling supported and empowered.
Why Parents Choose Claremont for Performing Arts
Choosing the right school is one of the most important decisions you will make for your child, especially when their passion runs as deeply as performing arts. If you want a community that understands that passion and nurtures it seriously, come and see Claremont for yourself. Visit the facilities, meet the team, and watch the students in action.

Independent education represents a significant investment for families and our bursaries are awarded up to 30% of tuition fees. What is a scholarship?
A scholarship is the recognition of academic, sporting, or artistic excellence, following assessment by Claremont School.
Scholars receive a reduction on school fees, opportunities to develop further in the areas that a scholarship is awarded, and, most importantly, tailored coaching and support in the respective areas of the award offered.
How much is a scholarship award worth?
Scholarships tend to be awarded to a maximum of 15% of tuition fees.
What is a difference between a scholarship and a bursary?
Both give financial assistance but are completely separate in their assessment.
Scholarship awards are given to pupils who have demonstrated excellence and ability in their chosen scholarship area.
A bursary can be given in recognition of financial need and can be applied for on behalf of any pupil who is registered with the School, regardless of ability. A bursary can also supplement a scholarship award amount. Bursaries are means-tested, so parents are asked to complete a financial circumstances form which is then assessed by the Principal.
What is the point of a scholarship?
Being awarded a scholarship is an honour for a student that will stay with them for life. It also allows them to access special programmes in each discipline with specialist teaching, trips and opportunities available to scholars that are not available to others.
What are the fees for applying for a scholarship?
In order to apply for a Year 7, Year 9 or Year 12 scholarship a non-refundable application fee of £50.00 is required.

Yes, scholarships are available to all students. Awards are made for tuition fees only.

Claremont School is celebrating excellent A Level and BTEC results, with students securing places at a diverse range of destinations.
Claremont School is celebrating excellent A Level and BTEC results, with students securing places at a diverse range of destinations. The results reflect not only strong academic achievement, but the breadth of pathways Claremont opens up for every student, regardless of their starting point. Students taking our BTEC qualifications in 2026 have achieved over 2 grades higher than that predicted by aptitude testing, which is testament to their hard work and the personalised support each student receives in our Sixth Form.

Destinations in this cycle are Law and Biological Sciences at Surrey, Politics at Exeter, Film & TV Production at Falmouth, Psychology at UCL, Architecture at Kingston, Acting at LMA and a media apprenticeship. From competitive Russell Group offers to specialist vocational routes, Claremont students are moving forward into higher education and employment with genuine confidence in the direction they have chosen. Claremont School has long believed that qualifications alone are not enough to guarantee success in today's rapidly changing educational and workplace environment. As employers increasingly prioritise adaptability, resilience and character alongside technical knowledge, the School has placed equal emphasis on developing the skills and attitudes that allow students to turn academic achievement into lasting career success. Through its five pillars, performing arts programme and football academy, combined with alongside a rigorous academic curriculum, Claremont equips students with the confidence, curiosity and work ethic that universities and employers alike value so highlyare looking for.
“A holistic approach is central to what Claremont does best: identifying potential early, providing a platform for ambition, and supportingensuring that every student, whatever their starting point, in finding is able to find a pathway that is genuinely their own. The School's results this year are a clear demonstration of that philosophy in action.”
With the landscape of higher education and employment continuing to evolve, Claremont remains committed to preparing students not just to meet the demands of today's world, but to shape their own futures within it. The School's approach recognises that success looks different for every individual, and that a truly excellent education is one that can flex to support each student's unique ambitions.
Claremont extends its congratulations to every student receiving results this year, and to the staff and families who have supported them throughout their journey. The School looks forward to following their progress as they take the next step, whether that is at university, in an apprenticeship, or in the world of work.

Rising Stars - Outstanding GCSE Results at Claremont
Claremont School students celebrate outstanding GCSE results, with rising value added and improvements across every measure.
This year's cohort has delivered a very strong collective performance, with a significant rise in both the school's value added score and grade average, confirming that Claremont students are not simply achieving good grades, but consistently exceeding expectations relative to their starting points. Crucially, the improvement was not confined to a single headline figure: attainment, progress and the proportion of students achieving top grades all rose in step, reflecting a year of sustained hard work across every subject and every year group.
As ever, there are stories of individual success. For some it was achieving grade averages between 7.5 and 8.5. For others it was achieving 4s and 5s in areas where they thought they could never achieve. Success is relative and the school is proud of each and every student who has taken exams this summer. This summer has seen particular strength in Maths, English Language, Geography and PE, with Claremont’s traditional success in the Performing and Creative Arts once again replicated with outstanding grades.
Behind the numbers are hundreds of individual stories of ambition rewarded. This year's results have taken this cohort of students one step closer to a range of future careers: future doctors securing the grades that keep them on the path to medicine, engineers edging towards building the next generation of technology, dancers and artists growing in confidence and skill as they explore their creative boundaries. GCSEs are the first key academic landmark for children growing up and, whatever the final destination, Claremont's Y11 can leave this results day with real momentum as they head into the Sixth Form.
The School’s Principal, Ed Dickie commented: “What strikes me most about this year's results is not just the grades themselves, but the attitude that produced them. It has been a fabulous Y11. Our students have shown extraordinary ambition and resilience, and that spirit is exactly what will carry them through their next step into Sixth Form education. In a flash they will be choosing university, apprenticeship or career options; today, they are all one step closer to that moment and in a stronger place than they were yesterday. They now know more about who they are and what they can achieve.”
Claremont’s distinct learning approach emphasises the development of life skills and the opportunities that come outside the classroom as well as inside it. It will be these skills and experiences that turn great qualifications into successful lives and careers. Staff across the school have pointed to a genuine culture shift in recent times, with students taking greater ownership of their learning and setting their own ambitious targets. That drive, combined with high-quality teaching and a relentless focus on progress for every individual, has translated directly into results that speak for themselves.
As students celebrate today, the school is already looking ahead, with plans in place to build on this year's momentum and ensure the next cohort is given every opportunity to again take their own step closer to success.

UEFA A Licence Outfield | Former Arsenal First Team | England U21 International
Matt is a former professional footballer, progressed through Arsenal’s academy under Arsène Wenger before playing with the first team in the Premier League and enjoying a decade-long career at QPR with over 300 appearances as Captain. He has worked in football development internationally, launching Arsenal’s European academy in Greece, and helped Barnsley FC retain Championship status as first-team coach. Matt holds UEFA ‘A’ License with high-level football experience and extensive Global contacts.
Trevor is a highly experienced football professional and UEFA A licensed coach, with nearly 20 years in the professional game. He has worked with leading clubs including Arsenal and West Ham United, building extensive expertise across coaching, player development, and performance leadership. During this time, he has supported the development of top talent, including England internationals Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice. He also spent six years as Head of Football in the private Education sector, where he led programmes focused on elite development and long-term player progression.
MSc Strength & Conditioning Loughborough University | Former Leicester City coach
Jake holds an MSc in Strength and Conditioning from Loughborough University. A former strength and conditioning coach at Leicester City FC, he is working towards UKSCA and BASES accreditation. Jake specialises in applying sport science principles to optimise player performance and development.
UEFA A Licence Outfield and Advanced Youth Award | Former Arsenal, Manchester United and Brighton coach
Joe is a high-performance leader with experience at Arsenal, Manchester United, Brighton, Brentford, and Fulham. He’s worked with elite talent, including Bukayo Saka, and specialises in creating pathways to professional football, US Colleges, and UK Universities. Joe holds the UEFA A Licence, Advanced Youth Award and FA talent ID Level 4 in Leadership & Management.
UEFA A Licence Goalkeeping | Former Chelsea and West Ham Goalkeeper Coach
Neale has over 12 years of experience coaching goalkeepers at Chelsea, West Ham, and Charlton Athletic. He is currently a Goalkeeper Scout for Manchester City. Neale holds both the UEFA B Outfield and Goalkeeping Licences, underlining his expertise in goalkeeper development.
Sports Psychology Specialist
Tiggy is a sports psychology coach and counsellor specialising in resilience, confidence, and focus. She has worked across multiple sports, including elite experience with Saracens Rugby Club, and holds SEPAR accreditation with BASES. Combining one-to-one support, workshops, and counselling, Tiggy helps athletes enhance wellbeing, motivation, and performance.
Chartered Physiotherapist
Will is an MSc-qualified Chartered Physiotherapist and CEO of Wells Physiotherapy Clinic. He specialises in sports injury, rehabilitation, and return-to-play support. Will brings clinical expertise and a strong focus on athlete wellbeing.

Book a tour at Claremont School
Book a private tour of Claremont at a time and date that suits you. Our Admissions team our here to help with any queries or requests you may have before your visit.
Why visit us?
Supporting lifelong learning
Every child is seen, valued, and supported to achieve their potential — we embrace differences as strengths, with close personal support from experienced tutors and support staff.
Home-from-home boarding experience
Boarders gain independence and confidence in a safe, inclusive, home-from-home boarding family, in the beautiful East Sussex countryside.
Multilingual learning
Students fast-track English fluency while growing in their home languages with additional opportunities to learn French, Spanish, German or Mandarin.
Students build communication, digital-fluency and self-leadership through a life skills framework backed by Cambridge University and Camtree.
Technology enhanced learning
Prepare to succeed in a tech-driven world using the latest tools and software which enable students to learn, experiment and grow.
Award-winning performing arts programme
Students develop their skills through a double national award-winning programme with specialised training in music, dance and drama, leading to either an A Level, BTEC, LAMDA or ABRSM qualification.
International Football Academy
Boys and girls pursue their dreams on the field and all aspects of the grame through an intensive development programme with experienced coaches and professional facilities.
Where confidence grows
At our private independent school in East Sussex, students connect with peers around the world through global skill-building programmes and learning opportunities as part of the International Schools Partnership network.
Where to find us
All of our facilities are easily accessible either by car, by taking the A21 trunk road from the M25, or by train arriving at Etchingham (for Prep School) or St. Leonards Warrior Square (for boarding houses).
If arriving in the UK at Ashford International Station, families can take the train line to Hastings, a journey of approximately 40 minutes
